Subject: Performance roundtable: finalizing demo run order & contingency windows

Team / Tim,

Putting this thread together to lock the demo run order and explicit contingency windows for the Renton.ai performance deep-dive. We need a single authoritative schedule and a short list of preflight items so the exec demo stays within our latency and token-throughput targets.

Proposed primary window (PT):
- Dry run / canary: 2026-05-19 08:45 - 09:15
- Main demo window: 2026-05-19 09:30 - 11:30 (two 30m runs + buffer)
- Contingency / follow-up: 2026-05-19 11:30 - 12:30

Key asks:
- Marcus: confirm load config (batch sizes, seq lengths, target steady-state tokens/min and peak burst target).
- Olga: on-call infra lead & escalation plan (who will pages, runbooks to follow).
- Jasmine: observability dashboards and the exact trace spans we want captured (latency percentiles + KV miss rates).
- Tim / Renton: confirm attendee list and whether you want an earlier canary (30m) with your SRE team in the loop.

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf (latest run order), load-config.yaml.

If youan confirm by EOD Mon (05/17) Ian send the calendar invite + attach the canary checklist.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Program Manager, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance roundtable: finalizing demo run order & contingency windows

Ava / team,

Quick notes from infra/serving side after reviewing runbook_v2 and load-config.yaml:
- Baseline config: sequences = 512 tokens, request pattern = bursty interactive (p95 response target), steady-state payload mix (70% gen short, 30% long-form).
- Throughput targets for the demo: steady-state ~120k tokens/min (2k tokens/sec aggregated across the pool). Prepare for spikes up to 300k tokens/min (~5k tokens/sec) for stress scenario during the second run.
- Batching: we'll use dynamic batching with max batch = 32; please ensure client-side concurrency is capped to avoid huge batch latency amplification.
- KV cache: prewarm keyspaces for the demo corpus; expect cold-miss penalties on first 10k tokens. Olga: we need a plan to prepopulate caches ~30m before the canary.
- Quantization: use q4_0 variant for the demo models to reduce GPU memory pressure; performance regression is within acceptable demo tolerances.

Ian own the load generator config and will push a validated load-config.yaml to the Drive link this afternoon.

Marcus
Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Thanks all or confirmations. Final schedule and action items below - I
m sending the GCal invite now (link below).

Final schedule (PT) - 2026-05-19:
- 08:45 - 09:10: Canary dry-run (Renton SRE on call) - short spike + baseline verification
- 09:30 - 10:00: Demo run #1 (interactive scenarios) - steady-state target
- 10:15 - 10:45: Demo run #2 (stress & burst profile) - 5-minute 300k tokens/min spike inside this slot
- 11:00 - 11:30: Latency/trace readout & quick follow-ups

Action owners: 
- Marcus: finalize load-config.yaml and upload to Drive by EOD 5/18 (I see a draft there already).
- Olga: prewarm KV cache 30m prior to 08:45; ops pager = olga.petrov@redwood.com and +1-555-0103 (during demo).
- Jasmine: dashboard links and p95/p99 traces; attach to the calendar event.
- Tim / Renton: confirm final attendee list in calendar invite.

Contingency plan (short):
- If canary shows >15% degradation on p95, we abort main run and fall back to reduced load (50%) for readout-only.
- If GPU OOMs occur, we
 drop to q4_1 model and run a single readout pass.

Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=perf-demo-20260519-ava
Drive runbooks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPerfRunbooks
